# AHU-3 sequence review: findings for the engineer

The issues are in priority order. IDs are review IDs (RV-nn). The original has no FR-IDs, so no requirement can be traced to a test yet.

## A. Life safety and equipment protection

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| RV-01 | §6 Smoke detector | SD-3 stops SF-3 "through the BAS". Fan shutdown on smoke must not depend on a software path (NFPA 90A, local fire code). The restart is also vague: acknowledging an alarm does not confirm the smoke condition is cleared. | Hardwire SD-3 to the fan motor starter or VFD run circuit. Have the BAS monitor the status only. Require a manual reset at the detector or fire alarm panel, then a BAS restart command. Reference the fire alarm interface and the SIS/life-safety documents. Confirm with the AHJ. |
| RV-02 | §5 Freezestat | Auto restart above the restart temperature is unsafe. A cycling fan with a frozen or stalled coil can burst the coil. The sequence also does not command the valves. | Make FZ-3 a hardwired, manual-reset trip. On a trip, drive HV-3 open, stop the pump or enable freeze protection, and alarm. Move the trip and reset values to the setpoint list. |
| RV-03 | §7 Power loss | "Valves stay in last position" is not a defined fail position. It is a hazard for the HV-3 freeze case. It is also a humidity problem in Houston, because an open CV-3 with the fan off is an unplanned state. There is no restart behavior. | Define the fail position for HV-3, CV-3 and the OA damper in a fail-position table. Define power-return behavior: state, delays, and staggered restart. Add comms-loss and controller-fault behavior. |
| RV-04 | Whole document | No SF-3 proof (status, current switch, differential pressure). No high-static or low-static cutout. No damper end-switch proving before the fan starts. Nothing covers fan or VFD fault. | Add a start sequence with a step table: Step, Action, Transition, Timeout, Failure response. Add a stop sequence. Reference the cause-and-effect chart for interlocks. |

## B. Houston humidity and control logic

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| RV-05 | §3 Economizer | A dry-bulb-only enable at 75 F lets in humid air in Houston (dew points often above 70 F). It would load the coil, raise space RH and risk condensation and mold. | Enable on enthalpy or dew point plus dry-bulb. Add a high-limit lockout and hysteresis. Ask the engineer for the design basis. |
| RV-06 | General | There is no dehumidification or humidity control. A 55 F DAT cools the air but does not control RH. Without reheat there is no way to dehumidify and hold space temperature. | Add a space or return RH/dew-point control sequence and an RH sensor tag. Add a reheat or coil-leaving-air strategy, and state which valve or coil does it. If the design intends none, record that as an explicit decision. |
| RV-07 | §2 Unoccupied | Only a low-temperature heating call is defined. There is no humidity protection when the unit is off. Houston buildings need an unoccupied dew-point or RH override. | Add an unoccupied high-RH or dew-point start with a minimum run time. Confirm that the OA damper stays closed in that mode. |
| RV-08 | §3 and §4 | Both the MAT and the DAT are given a 55 F setpoint. The economizer holds MAT at 55 F while the coil holds DAT at 55 F. At 55 F MAT the cooling coil has nothing to do, so the loops conflict or hunt. The economizer cannot reach 55 F MAT when the OA is near 75 F. | Define one controlling variable per device. Typical choice: DAT controls the coils, and the economizer modulates to a separate, different MAT setpoint. Put the values in the setpoint list. |
| RV-09 | §4 Single PID | The 0–50% / 50–100% split range has no deadband between heating and cooling. This is a known source of simultaneous or hunting heating and cooling. Anti-windup and a minimum-position rule are not defined. The split-range point (50%) also ties heating to cooling gain. | Use separate heating and cooling outputs, or define a deadband around the transition. State what happens in each mode, including reset. Keep tuning out of the narrative. |
| RV-10 | §3 Economizer | There is no hysteresis, no lockout, and no definition of the OA damper relationship with the 20% minimum. | Add enable/disable hysteresis and min-position rules. State which signal wins, minimum OA or economizer. |

## C. Laboratory-specific gaps

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| RV-11 | §1 and §3 | A lab AHU often serves 100% outside air, in which case an economizer and a 20% minimum do not apply. The document does not say whether AHU-3 has return air or mixes. | Ask the engineer: 100% OA or mixed? Add an air-flow diagram and the return or exhaust interface. |
| RV-12 | §1 | Minimum OA is a fixed damper position. Lab ventilation is set by air changes and by fume hood exhaust makeup, not by damper percent. | Control OA to a measured airflow tag. Reference the lab ventilation basis and the exhaust interface. |
| RV-13 | §1 Static | There is a fixed duct static setpoint, with no reset. Lab VAV and hood loads vary, so a fixed setpoint wastes fan energy. It also gives no high-limit trip. | Specify static reset by damper demand, or confirm a fixed setpoint is intended. Add a high-static cutout. |
| RV-14 | §2 Unoccupied | The unoccupied sequence does not mention minimum lab air change rate or space pressurization. These often must continue 24 hours. SF-3 off plus an OA damper closed may violate the pressure relationship. | Confirm the unoccupied air change rate and pressure requirement with the owner and the lab EHS group. |
| RV-15 | General | No building or space pressure relationship (cascade) is defined. | Add pressure relationship and offset tags, or reference the lab airflow controls document. |

## D. Document quality (testability)

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| RV-16 | All | No requirement IDs and no test method. Nothing can be traced to FAT. | Number each requirement as FR-AHU3-NNN and add a test method. |
| RV-17 | §1–§5 | Numbers sit in prose: 06:00–18:00, 1.5 in. w.c., 20%, 60 F, 75 F, 55 F, 38 F, 40 F. | Move all values to a setpoint list. Cite them by name. |
| RV-18 | General | No state table. Modes (occupied, unoccupied, warm-up, cool-down, freeze trip, smoke trip, humidity override) and their transitions are implied, not defined. | Build the state and transition table first. Show permissives, initiator, and automation level. |
| RV-19 | General | No startup or shutdown sequence, no morning warm-up or cool-down, and no schedule override or holiday. | Add these as sequence tables with timeouts. |
| RV-20 | General | No bad-PV or sensor failure behavior for SAT, MAT, space temperature, static, or OA temperature or humidity. No comms loss from the BAS. | Add an abnormal-handling table: failure, detection, substitute value or action, alarm. |
| RV-21 | General | No alarms listed (filter, fan fail, high or low temperature, freezestat, smoke). | Reference the rationalized alarm database. Do not restate it. |
| RV-22 | General | There are no tag numbers for several points: space temperature, OA temperature and humidity, MAT, DAT, static pressure, damper actuators. | Reference the instrument index and add missing tags. |
| RV-23 | Language | Sentences such as "when the temperature rises above 40 F" do not say which sensor. "Operator" and "BAS" are used loosely. | Name the tag in each instruction. Apply an STE edit last, after the content is settled. |

## E. Questions to send the engineer (open items)

| ID | Question | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-1 | 100% OA or mixed air? (RV-11) | ME | TBD |
| OI-2 | Dehumidification and reheat intent, with RH limits (RV-06) | ME | TBD |
| OI-3 | Economizer enable basis: enthalpy or dew point (RV-05) | ME | TBD |
| OI-4 | Fail positions for HV-3, CV-3, and OA damper (RV-03) | ME | TBD |
| OI-5 | Smoke and freeze hardwiring and reset method (RV-01, RV-02) | ME, Electrical, AHJ | TBD |
| OI-6 | Unoccupied air change and pressure requirements (RV-14) | ME, Owner EHS | TBD |

Owners and due dates are placeholders. I did not have names or a schedule, so please assign them.

**Suggested priority before programming:** resolve RV-01 to RV-05 and RV-08 first. Each affects either safety, wiring, or the basic control architecture.
